restatements.text: Increases the state minimum wage to $17.00 per hour beginning January 1, 2028.

evidence.quote: the state minimum wage increases to $17.00 per hour.
evidence.why: The text raises the legal minimum wage floor, directly strengthening worker pay requirements.

evidence.quote: the state minimum wage increases to $17.00 per hour.
evidence.why: Raising the minimum wage increases direct labor costs for businesses that currently pay employees less than the new rate.

analysis.answer: Current law sets the state minimum wage at $15.00 per hour. The measure increases it to $17.00 per hour starting January 1, 2028.
Employers will face increased direct labor costs to pay workers the higher wage. There may be opportunity costs if businesses reduce hiring, investment, or hours to offset the higher payroll.
Employers bear the direct cost of the higher wages. Consumers may bear some cost if businesses raise prices. Workers currently earning less than $17.00 per hour benefit from increased pay.

Employers might respond by raising prices, reducing employee hours, automating certain tasks, or accepting lower profit margins. Workers may remain at their jobs longer, potentially reducing turnover.

The measure addresses the challenge of low-wage workers meeting the cost of living. The mechanism sets a legally binding minimum wage floor. This creates a risk of perverse incentives, such as employers reducing hours or hiring to offset increased costs.
Workers earning below the new minimum wage gain concentrated benefits, while costs are spread across employers and potentially consumers.

The effect of minimum wage increases on employment is disputed. Some research finds that higher minimum wages lead to reduced employment or fewer hours worked, especially for low-skill workers. Other research finds minimal to no negative employment effects, highlighting substantial income gains for low-wage workers and reduced employee turnover.
Administrative and enforcement costs for state labor agencies may slightly increase to update materials and investigate compliance with the new rate.

flags.note: Sets a delayed effective date for the wage increase.
